Brahmapurāṇa
Counted a. the first among the Mahāpurāṇas; hence known also a. Ādipurāṇa; interlocution Lomaharṣaṇa an. the sages; from the absence of quotations from this Purāṇa in the works of early nibandha writers an. the cotnents of the present purāṇa text agreeing with the contents of a. Upapurāṇa of the same name a. referred to by Narasimha Vājapeyin, this text is held a. apocryphal; compiled between 10th an. 12th century. See R. C. Hazra, Purāṇic Record on Hindu rites an. customs, p.. 145-57.
The Gautamīmāhātmya in chs. 70-176 constitutes a. independent work by itself describing the sacred places an. temples. The Uttarakhaṇḍa in some mss. is said to be a description of the sacred river Balajā. See Wint. HIL. I. p. 535. For a brief account see Wilson, Viṣṇupurāṇa Intro. For a. analysis of the work see JRAS. V. p. 65.
The Purāṇa is said to have three different layers. The Purāṇa is a conglomeration of chs. corresponding to those of Viṣṇupurāṇa, Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa, Śāmbapurāna, Vāyupurāṇa, Harivam3śa an. Mahābhārata (Anuśāsana; Śānti--parvans).
For a detailed study see Surabhi H. Trivedi, J. of Ori. Inst. M. S. Uni. Baroda XVIII. p.. 74-100. [Page173-a.
ment. in Kūrmapurāṇa, Oxf. 88; Devībhāgavata, Oxf. 79b; Revāmāhātmya, Oxf. 65a; Varāhapurāṇa, Oxf. 59a; Vāmanapurāṇa, Oxf. 45b an. by Hemādri in Pariśeṣakhaṇḍa, 1. 1552, 1553, 1556.
